This was a rough week. All 12 major funds and all 11 sectors fell, SPY lost 8.6% and QQQ 10.5%, and the VIX nearly doubled from 19.3 to 35.9, its highest close of the past year. Tech took the worst of it, down 12.5% this week and 19.6% over the month.

The year's pattern held, and the gap got wider. Consumer staples fell only 2.0% and are still up 18.7% this year, and the value fund is up 13.9% while the growth fund is now down 6.6%. Equal weight, dividend and small-cap value funds all fell less than the S&P 500.

Treasuries were the place people ran to, not gold or crypto. The 10-year yield fell 24 bps to 4.91%, and over 20 days stocks trailed Treasuries by 9.8 points. Gold dropped 8.9% and Bitcoin 13.5%, and the high-yield spread widened to 3.52%, above its 2.90% 1-year average.

Keep an eye on the VIX. At 35.9 it is in the method's High zone, which it calls historically one of the most reliable entry windows, and it now sits above the 3-month VIX. Individual investors actually got less bearish (42.2%, from 51.4%), but that survey closed on Wednesday, before the week was done, so next week's reading will say more.
